title: Pirates
strapline: Sail the high seas and discover treasure together.
intent: Introduce role‑play and storytelling through pirate adventures.
Develop spatial language – up, down, over, under – as children navigate the ship.
Encourage cooperation as crews work together to hoist sails and find treasure.
Build fine‑motor skills with rope‑tying and map‑making activities.
Expand vocabulary of sea‑related words and sounds.
implementation: Create a simple ship area with cardboard, fabric sails and a steering wheel.
Provide treasure maps for children to follow, using simple symbols.
Offer rope loops and fabric strips for children to practice knot‑tying.
Play sea‑shanty songs and encourage children to add their own verses.
Use a treasure chest filled with safe objects for discovery moments.
key_questions: Where does the treasure lie on the map?
How do we steer the ship to avoid rocks?
What sounds does the ocean make?
Can you show me how to tie a simple knot?
What would you name your pirate crew?

impact.text: Children use directional language while moving around the ship area.
Children practice fine‑motor skills tying rope loops.
Children collaborate to follow a treasure map and locate hidden objects.
Children expand sea‑related vocabulary through songs and role‑play.
Children express imagination by creating their own pirate stories.

enhancements: Add a cardboard telescope for looking out to sea.
Include a sand‑filled ‘beach’ corner for digging treasure.
Provide costume pieces – hats, eye patches, scarves.
Create a simple ‘storm’ soundscape with wind recordings.
Introduce a treasure‑counting activity using shells.
Use a large map on the wall for whole‑group navigation.
Add a ‘parrot’ plush that repeats key words.

playing_exploring: Children explore the ship space with their whole bodies, climbing and crawling.
Babies feel the texture of rope and fabric, discovering sensory qualities.
active_learning: Children repeat knot‑tying steps, refining their technique each time.
Children count steps on the deck, practicing number language.
creating_thinking: Children invent their own pirate names and back‑stories.
Children design simple treasure maps with symbols.
